claim: All nutraceutical manufacturers, relabellers/brand owners, importers, and marketers in India must hold a 14-digit FSSAI License; almost no practical exemptions exist for nutraceutical firms.
stance_target: FSSAI licensing is mandatory for all entities in India's nutraceutical supply chain
scope_conditions: India; nutraceutical category (Category 13.6) under FSS Act 2006
quoted_support: All individuals associated with the food business of Health Supplements and Nutraceuticals such as the manufacture, rebranding, repackaging, and importation are required to hold an appropriate 14 digit FSSAI License in accordance with the FOOD SAFETY AND STANDARDS ACT, 2006.

claim: FSSAI license fees for nutraceuticals: State License ₹3,000-₹5,000/year (by production capacity); Central License ₹7,500/year; Basic Registration ₹100/year.
stance_target: FSSAI regulatory compliance cost context for Indian nutraceutical brands
quoted_support: Registration (Basic) ₹100 per year; State License ₹3,000 - ₹5,000 per year (depending on production capacity); Central License ₹7,500 per year

claim: FSSAI license validity ranges from 1 to 5 years at the FBO's discretion, renewable via FoSCoS Portal up to 30 days before expiry.
stance_target: FSSAI license renewal requirements for Indian nutraceutical brands
scope_conditions: India; all FSSAI-licensed Food Business Operators
quoted_support: The validity period of a License issued under the Act shall extend to a minimum period of 1 year and a maximum period of 5 years. The choice of validity period shall be in the hands of the Food Business Operator.

claim: Nutraceutical FSSAI applicants must submit a recall plan as a mandatory document, showing how defective batches would be recalled — mandatory for Category 13.6.
stance_target: India nutraceutical regulatory compliance requires batch recall capability
quoted_support: Recall Plan: A mandatory document showing how you would recall defective batches.

claim: The FSSAI's nutraceutical regulations specifically distinguish between 'food' and 'drug', ensuring products marketed as health supplements cannot make disease treatment/cure claims.
stance_target: Indian regulatory framework prevents nutraceuticals from making medicinal claims
scope_conditions: India; nutraceutical and health supplement category
quoted_support: FSSAI has played a vital role in distinguishing between 'food' and 'drug.' It makes sure that products such as Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, and Functional Foods are fit for consumption without any misleading cure claims.
